[engine] A capped diagnostic readback must be gated on the PHASE that contains the question, not merely on the knob that arms it. If the probe is counter-limited, the first N graphs of a process are warmup and prefill; numbering 'graph 3' across the whole process addresses a graph where the mechanism under test may not even be running. Gate on the phase (batched vs not) and print the ordinal inside that phase.

<!-- lesson_id: eng-mh-0011 | class: measurement-hygiene | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `measurement-hygiene`

## 為什麼（because）

The ffn_moe_down output capture was first written with `static int cgc_s1_out_n = 0; if (cgc_s1_out_n < 6)` around a loop that dumps every captured layer. graph_compute is called for every graph, so that budget is consumed by the first six graph computes of the process -- warmup and prefill chunk processing -- before the first decoded token exists. Prefill takes a different branch of the expert-cache hook entirely (it builds no remap leaf; the hook itself checks n_tokens), so the arms would have been compared at a graph where the S1 mechanism under test is not engaged, and the comparison would have reported 'identical' for a reason that has nothing to do with the mechanism. The fix is one line of predicate: the second parameter of graph_compute is `batched` (= ubatch.n_tokens > 1), so `if (cgc_s1_outcap && !batched)` both spends the budget on decode graphs and makes the printed ordinal an honest address within the phase being discussed.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

A 6-graph readback budget spent entirely on warmup and prefill, in a probe whose stated purpose was to compare one decode graph between two arms.
